text:
sre_bot: ALERT: auth-service 5xx spike in us-west-2 (error_rate 48% over 5m) — source=auth-prod-*.svc
alex: Oncall here. Looking. Any deploys in the last hour? @devon
devon: Pushed a scheduled key rotation job ~40m ago to rotate JWKS keys; it was a DB-backfill + broadcast. Rollout was gradual (10%). No other infra changes.
maya: I'm auth lead — checking logs for unknown_kid / jwks mismatch. Getting a lot of `unknown_kid` and `key_parse_error` from auth-validator. Also seeing some 500s in token-introspect service.
support_bot: Multiple high-severity tickets filed: customers get 403/500 on API calls with valid API keys. Snippet from a support ticket:

lydia (customer): "We started getting 403s around 15:20 UTC, requests that previously worked now failing. Example curl attached. Can you confirm?"

alex: Can someone paste repro curl + response? Need to triage quickly.
maya: Repro (from prod-worker):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImtleS0yIn0..." https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Response headers/body:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "reason": "unknown_kid"
}
```

alex: Unknown_kid points to JWKS mismatch. Which nodes have the new keyset? maya: The rotation writes new keys to secret-store, then a fanout job tells auth instances to reload. I'm seeing half the auth pods fetched new keys, half still on old. There's a replication lag reported from secret-store: `replication_latency_ms=23000` during the window.

devon: There was a short DB master failover 39m ago in us-west-2. The rotation job started at ~38m ago and probably saw a partially restored topology. The fanout used the global pubsub and one of the fanout messages failed and retried; some instances never picked up the reload.

ops_oncall: That would cause mixed keysets; tokens minted before rotation reference old kid, those minted after reference new kid. But why 5xxs? Unknown_kid should be 401/403.

maya: We're also seeing a bug in the token-validator: when `jwks_fetch` fails it returns a 500 instead of gracefully rejecting with 401 and triggering JWKS refresh. So a stale-cache + fetch failure -> 500 cascade.

alex: OK mitigation plan — step 1: pause rotation rollout; step 2: force all auth instances to reload the canonical JWKS from the primary secret-store; step 3: reduce CDN/cache TTL on /.well-known/jwks.json and clear in-memory caches. devon: I can trigger reloads and purge CDN cache.

devon: Running command to force reload across auth ASG:
```
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=auth -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- pkill -HUP auth && echo reloaded $pod; done
```

maya: Also bumping jwks cache-ttl to 30s temporarily and invalidating local caches.

support_bot: Notifying affected customers: templated message drafted. Lydia, we've identified an auth key propagation issue and are rolling back to the previous keyset; expect recovery within ~10-15m. Will send update when resolved.

lydia (customer): Thanks for the quick reply — please keep me posted.

(5m pass — monitoring shows error rate dropping)

sre_bot: ERROR_RATE now 2.3% over 5m — trending down. 99th latency normalized.

alex: Confirming logs show `jwks_reload: success` across all auth pods. Running smoke tests.

maya: Smoke: token minting + validate: OK. Sample validate response now 200 with token payload. Example:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"sub":"user:1234","scope":"api:generate"}
```

devon: Rolling back the rotation job state in the DB to mark it 'rolled_back' and cleaned up partially written keys. Also captured the failed fanout message ID for debugging.

alex: Root cause summary (so far): key rotation coincided with a DB master failover; the rotation job created a partial keyset and the fanout to auth instances partially failed, leaving mixed JWKS across instances. A validator bug turned JWKS fetch errors into 500s causing a larger outage surface. CDN cache TTL for JWKS was too long so stale keys persisted in front of some instances.

jordan: Customer-impact summary for billing/outreach — how many customers? support_bot: Preliminary estimate ~24 customers had elevated errors during the 30m window; top 3 impacted are notified and offered credits.

alex: Next steps (actions):
- postmortem + timeline (owners: alex/maya)
- fix validator bug to treat unknown_kid/jwks-fetch failure as 401 with async refresh (owner: maya)
- make rotation fanout transactional / introduce two-phase commit or healthcheck (owner: devon)
- reduce CDN jwks TTL to 30s and add cache-invalidation hook to rotation (owner: devon)
- add canary strategy for rotations (owner: infra)
- run a chaos test to simulate DB failover during rotation (owner: eng-sre)
- customer follow-up & credits (owner: support)

maya: I'll start the roll-forward patch for validator behavior; will include a feature-flagged rollout.

alex: Good job everyone. Post-incident notes: please attach all logs and the fanout message trace to the incident ticket. We'll schedule a 60m postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Closing slack thread once postmortem doc is created.

support_bot: Update sent to affected customers at 16:12 UTC.

sre_bot: Final metrics: incident window 16:07 — 16:39 UTC, peak error_rate 48%, mean restoration time 22m. Incident severity: P2 (auth outage causing partial 403/500s)."
